Scientists at the institute have identified and corrected a common error that affects measurements of nanoscale structures using a widely used microscopy technique. The error arises when the tip of the instrument interacts with the sample surface in a way that alters the measured height, a problem that has long been recognized but rarely quantified. By comparing results with an independent reference method, the team developed a correction factor that can be applied to existing data. “Many published measurements may be off by as much as 20 percent,” said the lead author. The correction was described in a peer-reviewed paper and has been incorporated into free software available to the research community. The authors recommend that laboratories verify their procedures against the reference standards now offered by the institute.
